original_question: Let X be a proper geodesic Gromov hyperbolic space, let Gamma be a discrete cocompact subgroup of Isom(X), and let N be an infinite normal subgroup of Gamma. In this setting one knows that the exponential growth rate delta(N) satisfies delta(N) > (1/2) delta(Gamma). When is this lower bound sharp, and in particular do there exist normal subgroups N_i normal in Gamma such that delta(N_i) / delta(Gamma) tends to 1/2?
target_in_paper: Section 4 ("Cogrowth"), specifically Question 4.3, with your second sentence also overlapping the more specific Question 4.4. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient hyperbolic-space setting, the lower bound δ(N) > (1/2)δ(Γ), and the two issues the paper asks about: whether the lower cogrowth bound is optimal, and whether one can find normal subgroups whose critical exponents approach the half-bound. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))
missing_details: The paper’s δ(H) is the exponential orbit-growth rate (critical exponent) for the action H ↷ X, not just an unspecified abstract growth rate of the group H. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

The paper splits your draft into two official questions: Question 4.3 asks in general when the lower bound is sharp, while Question 4.4 asks the approximation-by-a-sequence question only under the extra hypothesis that Γ is a lattice in hyperbolic n-space H^n. Your draft broadens that second question beyond the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

For maximal fidelity to the paper, the second clause should be stated as δ(N_i) → δ(Γ)/2; your ratio formulation δ(N_i)/δ(Γ) → 1/2 is equivalent once δ(Γ) is fixed and positive, but it is not the paper’s own wording. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

The paper uses the terminology of cogrowth: in the special case where Γ is a free group and X is a Cayley tree, the quantity is the cogrowth of the quotient Γ/N. That context is omitted in the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

Because the known inequality is strict, 'sharp' here should be understood as optimality of the lower bound (for instance via approximating sequences), not literal attainment of equality within the stated theorem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))
refined_question: Let X be a proper geodesic Gromov hyperbolic space, let Γ < Isom(X) be a discrete cocompact subgroup, and for each subgroup H ≤ Γ let δ(H) denote the exponential orbit-growth rate (critical exponent) of the action H ↷ X. It is known that every infinite normal subgroup N ◁ Γ satisfies the lower cogrowth bound δ(N) > (1/2)δ(Γ). When is this lower bound optimal? More specifically, in the paper’s special geometric case, if Γ is a lattice in real hyperbolic space H^n, does there exist a sequence of infinite normal subgroups N_i ◁ Γ such that δ(N_i) → δ(Γ)/2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s intent, but it merges two adjacent official formulations and makes the second one broader than the paper does. Section 4 introduces the precise setting and the meaning of δ in terms of exponential growth for the action on X, then Question 4.3 asks generally when the lower bound is sharp, and Question 4.4 asks the existence-of-a-sequence question only for lattices in H^n. The refined question restores those hidden assumptions while staying as close as possible to the paper’s wording and scope. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))
